title: Spend-smoothing router for regional capacity and instance-class steering
creator: Aisha Nadar
description:
Problem: Customers are experiencing unpredictable unit cost spikes when our router aggressively prefers spot capacity in burst windows and when cross-region capacity is constrained. We need a routing layer that smooths spend against short-term volatility while preserving low-latency and graceful degradation.

Goal: Implement a spend-smoothing router module that: 1) allocates a time-windowed budget envelope per tenant/route/region, 2) scores instance-class candidates (spot/on-demand, GPU family) by perf-per-dollar + eviction risk + latency delta, 3) maintains hedged headroom (small pool of on-demand capacity or reserved instances) for high-priority traffic, and 4) supports automated model-variant degrade paths (quantized/distro models) when budget caps are hit.

Key behaviors: time-weighted spend forecast (EMA) to avoid overreacting to short spikes; probabilistic spot preference adjusted by predicted eviction probability; instance-class affinity scoring that factors in KV cache affinity (warm cache penalty), quantization compatibility, and cold-start cost; hard and soft caps: soft cap triggers probabilistic throttling and model-variant fallback, hard cap triggers circuit-breaker and direct on-demand fallback for SLA-bound customers.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement console UI for per-customer budget overrides (follow-up), nor full multi-tenant billing reconciliation. It focuses on router decision logic, simulation harness, and a safe rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Router exposes per-route/region budget envelope config and respects soft/hard caps in simulated and canary runs
P99 latency increase across 24h canary <= 8% and 95th percentile tokens-per-request cost reduced vs baseline under bursty load by >= 12%
Spot-preference decisions reduce eviction-induced fallback rate by >= 30% vs naive spot-first policy in historical-sim playback
Model-variant fallback engages automatically under soft cap with no data leak and correctness preserved for structured outputs
Observability: per-decision telemetry (reason, score components), budget burn-rate charts, and automated alerts when hard cap proximity > 90%
comments: 2026-02-20 — Design review with PM/Infra. Decided to use EMA window of 15 minutes for spend smoothing (configurable per-customer). Action: add simulation harness for 90-day historical traffic playback. — Aisha Nadar

2026-02-26 — Started implementation: added scoring proto for instance-class candidates (fields: perf_per_dollar, eviction_risk, cache_affinity, cold_start_penalty). Early microbench shows scoring compute adds ~120 microseconds per request decision in current prototype. — Benji Lowe

2026-03-03 — Simulation results (90-day replay, mixed workloads): naive spot-first policy cost=baseline; spend-smoothing policy reduced 7-day rolling cost spikes by 18% and decreased cascade fallbacks during region outages. Noted higher token-cost for short tails when smoothing horizon > 60m. Need to tune EMA window and soft-cap thresholds per workload class. — Simulation bot

2026-03-05 — Security/infra note: hedged headroom requires a small API to reserve on-demand capacity in Dedicated pools; blocked until Dedicated API for soft reservations is available or until we implement tokenized warm-pool bookkeeping. Raised dependency: ENG-74200 (internal). — Benji Lowe

2026-03-08 — Review feedback from Research: include quantization-compatibility into scoring (some models degrade too much on int8 fallback). Added a compatibility penalty for model-variant fallback. Also must expose per-model quality budget so PMs can tune graceful degradation. — Dr. Elena Park

2026-03-10 — Integration tests running: deployed canary to Canary cluster (5% of traffic). Observability dashboard (linked) shows decision reasons and per-customer budget burn. Early anomaly: one tenant with highly spiky traffic hit soft cap repeatedly and experienced too-frequent model swaps — plan: introduce minimum dwell time between variant switches. — Benji Lowe

2026-03-12 — Blocker: HUD for automatic reserve requests to Dedicated is still in review. Risk: without a warm on-demand buffer our fallback latency for P0 customers could exceed SLOs during a correlated spot eviction. Mitigation: temporarily bump:on-demand preference weight for P0 routes; follow-up tasks created. — Aisha Nadar
implementation_notes: Scoring pipeline will be executed inside the router decision service. Keep decision idempotent and cache scores per-request-id for replay. Use feature flags: feature.smoothing.enabled, feature.headroom.reserve-api, feature.variant-fallback. Persist per-tenant budget state in the existing kv-store with TTL aligned to window size. Expose a metric: routing.budget.burn_rate{tenant,region,route} and tracing tag routing.decision.reason.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: correlated spot evictions across multiple regions could exhaust hedged headroom; mitigation: global circuit-breaker and fallback to smaller model variants. Risk: too-aggressive smoothing can hide genuine demand growth; mitigation: detection rule for sustained burn-rate increase > 3x baseline triggering operator notification and automated temporary capacity allocation. Documented tradeoffs in design doc.
next_steps: Unblock Dedicated reservation API or implement temporary warm-pool bookkeeping (owner: infra)
Tighten EMA window tuning per workload class and add minimum dwell time for model-variant swaps
Run 4-week canary with progressive rollout (5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) and automated guardrail runbooks
Add console exposure for per-customer soft/hard cap overrides (follow-up PM ticket)
